newsitem.title: USA: Franklin Mint stops shipping unauthorized Tiger Woods medal.
newsitem.headline: Franklin Mint stops shipping unauthorized Tiger Woods medal.

text.p: In response to a request by Tiger Woods for a restraining order, Franklin Mint has agreed to temporarily stop advertising and shipping an unauthorised commemorative medal bearing the golf star's likeness, his publicist said Thursday.

A court hearing will be scheduled in Los Angeles for the golfer to receive an order prohibiting Franklin Mint from continuing to infringe upon Woods' trademark and publicity rights during the pending lawsuit, the publicist said.
Franklin Mint, which makes collectible plates, ornaments, dolls and other items, agreed to stop further advertising and shipping of the medal until the court hearing, she said.
Woods' representatives filed the order on Wednesday after Franklin Mint began shipping the medal despite a pending lawsuit by the golfer against the Philadelphia-based company, the statement said.
Franklin Mint officials were not immediately available for comment.

According to the lawsuit, filed earlier this month in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles, Woods sought the court order to force the company to destroy any medals still in stock and to pay him unspecified damages.

According to the complaint, Franklin Mint officials tried to get Woods' permission to use his likeness on a medal to commemorate the 21-year-old star's record-setting Masters victory, but it was refused.

The defendants, however, ran advertisements in major newspapers selling the souvenir medal "honoring golf's new master" for $37.50. The ads created the "false impression that Tiger Woods is in some manner associated or affiliated with the medal," the complaint said.
The medal is described as "low-end merchandise of the type with which Tiger Woods does not wish to associate himself."
Woods is also requesting an accounting of sales of unauthorised merchandise, for money damages and legal fees, his publicist said.

Woods, who has enjoyed a meteoric rise to the top of the golf world since turning professional last year, has struck multi-million dollar endorsement deals with a select group of companies, including Nike, Rolex and American Express.
Franklin Mint, owned by Lynda and Stewart Resnick, has annual revenues of $1.46 billion, Woods' publicist said.
